subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw apply to externally or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs before they can run on an inherited model?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes operator consent, shipped cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model cost policy, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
options.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring externally/plugin-registered agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Narrow model-cost warning only
options.body: Keep current activation semantics but warn or block when a recurring agentTurn job inherits an expensive default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Defer to separate guardrail issues
options.body: Resolve only #14376, #42475, and #71712 independently, accepting that consent, model-cost, and provenance may remain split.

recommendation.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring externally/plugin-registered agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS already routes the central cron job service file and security-sensitive paths to this team, and the decision is a security boundary.
